speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. Can you describe the specific movements you've been experiencing and how long they have been going on? Also, have you started any new medications recently?

speaker: Patient
text: 23-year-old college student. The patient is here for a follow-up appointment. He was recently diagnosed with schizophrenia and started on risperidone approximately 2 months ago. Reports a significant improvement in psychiatric symptoms since the start of treatment.

speaker: Doctor
text: Have you noticed if the movement disorder involves restlessness or an inability to sit still? I also need to check for any muscle stiffness or tremors to rule out acute dystonia or parkinsonism.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Inability to remain still, persistent feeling of restlessness. I also have Frequent fidgeting, Repetitive crossing and uncrossing of legs, Pacing. To keep my notes clear, please give only one final answer and keep it to a single direct conclusion.

speaker: Doctor
text: This clinical picture is classic for akathisia, a common side effect of antipsychotics like risperidone characterized by inner restlessness and an urge to move. DIAGNOSIS READY: Akathisia
